description: Every player in the player table is counted and ranked. Players without manager award records count as zero.

a.request: For every player in the `player` table, including those with no manager award records (counted as zero), give the `player_id`, the number of `manager_award` records they have, and that number as a fraction of the total of those counts across all players (unrounded; return nothing if that total is missing). Sort by the fraction from highest to lowest, with missing values last, and show only the first 10 rows.
a.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT COUNT(*) as total_count FROM manager_award) SELECT p.player_id, COUNT(ma.player_id) as award_count, CAST(COUNT(ma.player_id) AS FLOAT) / t.total_count as fraction FROM player p LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON p.player_id = ma.player_id CROSS JOIN totals t WHERE t.total_count > 0 GROUP BY p.player_id, t.total_count ORDER BY fraction DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each player in the player table (including those with zero manager_award records), calculate the count of manager awards and divide by the total manager award count across all players, then return the top 10 rows (player_id, count, fraction) sorted by fraction descending with nulls last.
d.sql: WITH total_awards AS (SELECT COUNT(*) as total_count FROM manager_award), player_awards AS (SELECT p.player_id, COUNT(ma.award_id) as award_count FROM player p LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id) SELECT pa.player_id, pa.award_count as count, CASE WHEN ta.total_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE pa.award_count::NUMERIC / ta.total_count END as fraction FROM player_awards pa CROSS JOIN total_awards ta ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

b.request: For each player in the player table, count their manager_award records (zero for players with no awards), calculate each player's fraction of the total manager award count, display player_id, count, and fraction sorted by fraction descending with nulls last, limited to top 10 rows.
b.sql: SELECT p.player_id, COUNT(ma.player_id) as count, COUNT(ma.player_id)::FLOAT / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM manager_award) as fraction FROM player p LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
b.raw: For each player in the player table, count their manager_award records (zero for players with no awards), calculate each player's fraction of the total manager award count, display player_id, count, and fraction sorted by fraction descending with nulls last, limited to top 10 rows.

c.request: For each player, how many manager awards (`manager_award` records) do they have, and what fraction of the total of those counts across all players does that represent (unrounded; return nothing if that total is missing)? Show the `player_id`, the count and the fraction, sorted by the fraction from highest to lowest with missing values last, and keep only the top 10 rows. Every player in the player table is counted and ranked. Players without manager award records count as zero.
c.sql: WITH award_counts AS (SELECT p.player_id, COUNT(ma.player_id) as count FROM player p LEFT JOIN manager_award ma ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.player_id), total_stats AS (SELECT SUM(count) as total FROM award_counts) SELECT ac.player_id, ac.count, ac.count::NUMERIC / ts.total as fraction FROM award_counts ac CROSS JOIN total_stats ts WHERE ts.total IS NOT NULL AND ts.total > 0 ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
